content.topic: Iron deficiency in chronic heart failure
content.summary: List of references and key points from guideline/literature citations addressing prevalence, diagnosis, screening, and treatment of iron deficiency in heart failure, including a report that high soluble transferrin receptor is a measure of iron deficiency and a predictor of mortality.
key_points: Disordered iron homeostasis is associated with chronic heart failure and relates to anemia, exercise capacity, and survival.
Guidance on screening, diagnosis and treatment of iron deficiency in chronic heart failure (implementation of 2016 ESC HF guidelines).
Iron deficiency occurs across chronic inflammatory conditions and has international expert recommendations for definition, diagnosis, and management.
High soluble transferrin receptor levels in patients with heart failure indicate iron deficiency and strongly predict mortality.
Iron deficiency represents a significant burden in heart failure and influences skeletal muscle function.
